summary: Iteration 38 retest after main agent fixes: (1) CRM JWT-based isolation ported into the active router crm_module.py, (2) POST /api/clients refactored to accept dict and normalize ES/EN field names, (3) user_to_response excludes _id. ALL 14 backend tests PASSED (100%). All three previously-critical bugs are RESOLVED.

minor.issue: Endpoint now accepts an untyped `dict` and bypasses Pydantic validation. Works for normalization but loses strict input validation (no type/length checks for cif, postalCode, etc.). Consider re-introducing a Pydantic model with alias_generator to support both ES/EN aliases while keeping validation.

When no JWT is present, the `isAdmin` query parameter still defaults to True and acts as a fallback. Although JWT path overrides it, a client that simply omits Authorization can still spoof admin listing. Consider hardening: when JWT is missing AND no requestingUserId, return 401 instead of treating as admin.
Token is returned under `tokens.access_token` (snake_case). Frontend code should be consistent — worth re-verifying.

action_items: (Optional) Re-introduce Pydantic model for POST /clients with field aliases instead of raw dict, so type validation is restored while keeping ES/EN compatibility.
(Optional) Tighten /crm/contacts: require auth (return 401 when no JWT and no requestingUserId) to remove the residual `isAdmin=true` fallback that any unauthenticated caller can exploit.
Remove duplicate file /app/backend/routes/crm.py (dead code now that logic is in crm_module.py) to prevent future confusion.
critical_code_review_comments: JWT isolation in crm_module.py correctly uses `_get_user_or_none` (HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)) so legacy callers without token still work. Good pattern.

Server-side codigo normalization (uppercase + uniqueness check) on POST /clients works. Good. But uppercase happens AFTER duplicate check uses the same normalized value — verified in code (line 1048 normalizes then line 1050 queries). Correct.
POST /clients now stores _id and pops it before return. Good — no Mongo ObjectId leak.
crm_module.py POST /contacts now sets createdByUserId + createdByUsername + auto-assigns assignedToId to creator when missing. Verified end-to-end.
Two parallel CRM routers still co-exist on disk (routes/crm.py and routes/crm_module.py). Only crm_module is wired; crm.py is dead code. Delete or merge to avoid future regressions.
